title: The Problem of Induction in Epistemology
text:
The problem of induction questions whether reasoning from past observations to future predictions is logically justified. It highlights the gap between empirical regularity and necessary truth, prompting deep philosophical debate regarding causality.

Key skeptics include David Hume, who argued that there is no rational basis for assuming that the future will resemble the past; observed patterns are not guarantees of future continuity. Therefore, inductive reasoning relies ultimately on custom or habit rather than pure logical deduction.

This challenge forces epistemology to consider alternative justifications for scientific laws and general principles, moving discussions toward confirmation theory or pragmatic acceptance within scientific methodology.
